# Shepherd of Hermas Chapter 17 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)

**Translator:** SOPHIA | **Source:** Codex Sinaiticus (ch 1-31) / P.Mich. 130 (ch 32+), Shepherd of Hermas 17 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/SHE_017_page_001.jpg

---

## Vision 3, Chapter 9

**1** When she had finished all this she said to me, "Is there anything else you would like to see?" I was overjoyed and said, "Lady, I would very much like to see more." **2** She laughed and said, "Do you see the seven women surrounding the tower?" "Yes, I see them, my lady," I replied. "This tower," she said, "is supported by these seven women. **3** The first, who grips the tower with her hands, is Faith. Through her God's chosen ones are saved. **4** The second, dressed in a long robe and exceedingly beautiful, is Continence. She is the daughter of Faith. Whoever follows her will be blessed in their life, for they abstain from all evil deeds, believing that if they refrain from all evil desire they will inherit eternal life." **5** "And who are the others, my lady?" "They are daughters of one another in succession: the first is Faith; the second, Continence; the third, Simplicity; the fourth, Knowledge; the fifth, Innocence; the sixth, Reverence; the seventh, Love." **6** "And what part do they play in the lives of believers?" "Listen," she said. "Whoever follows these women and holds fast to their works will dwell in the tower with the saints of God. **7** And why are they called daughters of one another? Because Continence is born of Faith; Simplicity of Continence; Innocence of Simplicity; Reverence of Innocence; Knowledge of Reverence; and Love of Knowledge. Their works therefore are pure and holy and divine."

---

### Council Notes

The virtue genealogy in v. 7 is one of the most theologically creative passages in the Shepherd. The chain — Faith → Continence → Simplicity → Innocence → Reverence → Knowledge → Love — traces a complete moral formation program. Each virtue is only accessible through the one that precedes it.

"Love" (agape) as the final fruit of Knowledge is significant: the Shepherd shares with 1 John and Paul (1 Cor 13) the conviction that love is the culmination and crown of all virtues. But here it is reached through a specific developmental sequence, not simply given.

The tower being "supported" by the seven women reinforces the ch. 10-11 material: the Church is constituted by these virtues. Remove any one and the building is weakened.
